title: Principles of pharmacology
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Apply pharmacokinetics, dosing and half-life, pharmacodynamics, drug metabolism and interactions, autonomic drugs, antimicrobial principles, analgesics, toxicology and antidotes, adverse reactions, special populations and drug development.

weeks.10: Adverse drug reactions and medication safety
weeks.11: Special populations: pregnancy, children, older adults and kidney disease

blocks.deliverable: Compute a loading dose, a maintenance dose and the time to steady state.
Predict interactions from cytochrome P450 induction and inhibition.
Predict heart rate and pupil effects of autonomic drugs.
Week 7 midterm; compare antibiotic classes by mechanism and spectrum.
Adjust a dose for reduced kidney function.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Dosing and safety workshop: compute loading and maintenance doses, adjust for kidney function, and write a medication-safety checklist (study exercises only).
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
